newsitem.title: UK: Palmoil lower in Europe, consolidating ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: Palmoil lower in Europe, consolidating ahead of data.

text.p: Palm oil prices were slightly lower at midday in Europe, but the market appeared to be consolidating ahead of the PORLA report due for release at the weekend.
Traders said there had been a downturn in activity with little early trade reported.
"Palm oil has not been as active this morning as it has been during the last couple of days because people are now waiting to see the PORLA figures on Saturday," said one trader.
Traders said the surge in Chicago prices on Tuesday was not helping the market, with most players unwilling to take fresh positions while the U.S. market was in the grip of the fund managers.
Traders were also looking more at problems closer to home following the outbreak of swine fever in the Netherlands.
"We could see a cut back in demand for animal feed which will lead to less oil being produced, but that is a long way down the road yet," said a trader.
The Dutch government said on Monday it would buy and destroy 800,000 pigs which cannot be marketed due to a ban on transporting livestock.
However other industry sources said they did not think a cut in meal demand would make any difference.
"Most of the crushers are working to produce oil and although meal is very important, oil is their main consideration at present," said another trader.
Any cut back in demand for meal in the Netherlands would be short term and would amount to around five percent of sales of animal feed to the pig industry.
At midday soft oils were 0.25 to 0.50 guilders higher in tradeless markets.
Crude palm oil was $2.50 lower after Feb traded at $585, Mar at $577.50 and Apr/Jun at $572.50 a tonne cif.
Products were around $2.50 down after RBD palm oil fetched $568 for Mar and olein $595 and $593 for Mar, $590 for Apr and $582.50 and $582 for Apr/Jun.
Lauric oils were unchanged to $2.50 up.
